category_title: Students with non-compliant behavior and difficulty accepting instructions or consequences
minimal_context: Garth is sitting at his desk with a textbook and worksheet to complete his independent academic work.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Garth, please open your textbook and start working on the worksheet at your desk.

STUDENT: (Makes a loud buzzing noise with his mouth and stares at the wall) I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: You need to get started on your independent work now.

STUDENT: This is stupid and you can't make me do it! (Pushes the textbook aggressively across the desk)

TUTOR: If you don't complete the assignment, there will be consequences.

STUDENT: I don't care! Shut up! (Rips the worksheet in half and throws it on the floor)

options.A: Use a digital application to take notes, organize independent work, and archive past worksheet assignments, having the student manage these materials during the independent work sessions at his desk.
options.B: Represent information in various ways by including movement and physical activity to represent concepts from the textbook, incorporating these physical actions during the student's independent work sessions at his desk.
options.C: Have a tape recorder sound a bell every minute; when it sounds, have the student record whether he had positive interactions during the preceding interval by checking Yes or No on a sheet of paper at his desk.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the assigned worksheet and textbook tasks, requiring him to finish the independent work at his desk within a strict period.
